chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Trimming the nails and removing the moustache every Friday is a protection from vitiligo and insanity.

key_terms.الْبَرَصِ: Vitiligo (a skin disease causing loss of color)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of trimming nails and removing the moustache on Friday in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), framing Friday’s grooming as a ritual purification that mirrors the spiritual renewal of the day. The promise of protection from vitiligo and insanity reflects the Shia understanding of the holistic link between physical cleanliness (taharah) and mental-spiritual well-being (salamah). This practice underscores the Imam’s guidance in integrating mundane hygiene with divine safeguarding.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Trimming the nails, and taking (plucking) the moustache during every Friday is a safety from the vitiligo and the insanity’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
’Clipping fingernails and mustache every Friday is immunity from albinism and insanity.’”
